Daily Brief

Europe faces an acute climate-energy nexus crisis as Romania fully shut down its only nuclear power plant due to record-low Danube water levels, removing 20% of the country's electricity capacity and forcing reliance on imports [BBC, RFI, Le Monde]. This development coincides with France evacuating hundreds as wildfires spread through the Landes region amid an unprecedented fire season [France 24]. Meanwhile, US-China trade tensions escalated sharply as the White House accused over 40 countries—including India, Mexico, Canada, Japan, and South Korea—of helping China evade tariffs through transshipment, while President Trump announced tariffs up to 100% on imported drones citing national security [BBC, The Hindu, Le Monde]. In the Middle East, reports emerged of deteriorating conditions aboard the USS Lincoln after a record 260-day deployment supporting operations against Iran, with the USS George Washington now en route as a replacement [France 24, The Hindu]. On the African health front, the DRC's Ebola outbreak spread to a sixth province and is on pace to become the deadliest in history, having already claimed over 2,100 lives [The Guardian]. Japan meanwhile grappled with unprecedented rainfall in Chiba prefecture that killed at least six people and stranded thousands during the Bon holiday period [BBC, Al Jazeera].

Top Stories
01 Climate

Romania Shuts Down Only Nuclear Plant as Danube Hits Record Lows, Threatening Energy Supply

  • Romania began full shutdown of Cernavodă nuclear plant on August 13 after Danube water levels fell to 30-year lows, eliminating 20% of national electricity production
  • The plant's second 706MW reactor was disconnected from the grid following July shutdown of first reactor; restart not expected within 10 days
  • Authorities attempted emergency measures including sinking rock-filled barges into the river at a cost of over €2 million to divert water flow
  • Romania has called for 'responsible consumption' and will rely on wind, solar, coal, gas, and electricity imports to cover the shortfall

US Accuses Over 40 Countries of Helping China Evade Tariffs Through 'Shadow Transshipment Network'

  • White House report named India, Canada, Mexico, Japan, South Korea, and the EU among countries allegedly facilitating Chinese tariff evasion
  • Trade adviser Peter Navarro claimed transshipments cost American jobs and billions in revenue, estimating $30-300 billion in goods rerouted
  • Administration announced plans to deploy AI to detect and penalize transshipment practices
  • Chinese embassy rejected accusations, stating 'trade wars have no winners' and that agreements on transshipped goods should not harm third parties

03 Policy

Trump Announces Tariffs Up to 100% on Imported Drones Citing National Security

  • President Trump imposed 100% tariffs on drones over 25kg with 'national security capabilities' such as thermal cameras, and 25% on smaller drones
  • Decision targets an industry dominated by Chinese manufacturers and aims to encourage domestic production
  • Tariffs set to take effect September 3, 2026
  • FCC had previously warned of risks including unauthorized surveillance, data exfiltration, and direct UAS attacks

04 Society

DRC Ebola Outbreak Spreads to Sixth Province, On Track to Become Deadliest in History

  • Ebola has now spread to Bas-Uele province after a man traveled from Isiro and died in Buta, bringing affected provinces to six
  • Current outbreak has killed over 2,100 people from more than 4,500 cases, reaching this toll nearly three times faster than the 2014-16 outbreak
  • WHO Director General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus stated the outbreak will surpass the deadliest in history (11,000+ deaths) at current pace
  • No approved vaccines or treatments exist for the rare Bundibugyo strain responsible for this outbreak; Uganda has reported 20 cases in Kampala
